name: 花そば・料理 ゆう (Hana Soba Ryori Yuu)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free fryer or preparation area is mentioned in any source. Tempura (wheat batter) is a core menu item prepared in the same kitchen as all other dishes.
The house kaeshi (soy tare) is made with wheat-containing soy sauce, aged two months in-house, and used as the base for all dipping sauces and many broth dishes.
Virtually all soba broth and dipping sauces on the Tabelog menu listing explicitly contain dashi and soy sauce; wheat-free alternatives are not mentioned.

Dashi made from bonito (katsuo) and kombu is used across the entire menu including hot soups, noodle broths, oden, ankake sauces, and side dishes. Even tofu preparations (agedashi tofu, hot tofu) are served with dashi-based sauce.

No allergen menu, allergy-handling policy, or staff training for dietary restrictions is mentioned on the official website or any third-party review source reviewed. Phone reservation line is available (079-285-0888) and is the recommended channel for dietary queries.
Soba noodles themselves are made from buckwheat flour — the base noodle is gluten-free grain — so the wheat risk is in sauces and accompaniments, not the noodle itself.
The chilled plain soba (もりそば) served with dipping sauce on the side allows some control over sauce exposure, though the sauce still contains wheat-soy kaeshi.

name: はりかい 姫路城店 (Harikai Himeji-jo-ten)

claims.text: Fish and chips is a signature menu item and almost certainly uses wheat batter; no dedicated fryer is documented. Cross-contamination from shared frying oil is plausible.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is the baseline seasoning in a Japanese seafood bar. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are documented at this establishment.
The kitchen handles fish, shellfish, eel, and octopus exclusively. No plant-only preparation area is documented; vegan cross-contact is highly probable.

The owner speaks English and is described as attentive and personally engaged with customers. While no formal allergy protocol is documented, the owner's language ability means direct communication about dietary needs is more feasible than at most casual seafood stalls.
English-speaking owner makes it possible to have a real conversation about ingredients, which is significantly better than the norm for casual Japanese seafood bars.
English photo menu is available, reducing ordering uncertainty for foreign visitors.

name: 姫路の地酒と姫路おでん本舗 (Himeji no Jizake to Himeji Oden Honpo)

claims.text: Food-court oden environment with shared cooking surfaces; no information on separation of allergens. High cross-contamination risk assumed.

The signature ginger soy sauce dipping condiment contains wheat. Standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu) used in oden broth also contains wheat. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.
All oden items are simmered in fish-based dashi broth. No vegan broth alternative is indicated. Cross-contact with fish and meat products throughout the menu.
No allergy handling procedures or allergen menu have been documented across any source reviewed. Direct inquiry required before dining.
Fully non-smoking interior.

name: 姫路 酒肴魚寿司 (Himeji Shukosaku Uozushi)

claims.text: Fried items (fried oysters, fried squid tentacles, fried octopus, croquettes, anko karaage, beef menchi katsu) appear on the menu. A dedicated fryer separate from wheat-flour batters is not confirmed; shared-fryer cross-contamination must be assumed absent explicit confirmation.
Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is the default seasoning for sushi and sashimi. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is listed anywhere on the menu or official sources.

Fish-based dashi is used in miso soup served alongside set meals. All menu sections feature seafood; no plant-only dishes identified. Cross-contact with fish products throughout the kitchen is unavoidable.

No published allergen declarations or allergy-handling policy found across Tabelog, Hotpepper, or the Festa Building shop guide. Diners with serious allergies should call 079-222-0158 before visiting.
Fresh fish sourced daily from across Japan, prepared to order at the counter — individual pieces rather than pre-made rolls reduces some risk of hidden sauces, though soy sauce use remains standard.

name: 姫路 タコピィ (Himeji Takopii)

claims.text: The kitchen is a compact open counter producing wheat-flour takoyaki continuously all day. There is no separation of gluten-containing and gluten-free cooking surfaces; cross-contact is certain.

No ingredient list is published, but standard Japanese takoyaki batter and dashi tsuyu both typically incorporate wheat-containing soy sauce. The shop has not disclosed a wheat-free soy sauce substitute.

The dashi broth is made from four fish stocks (sand eel, bonito, skipjack tuna, mackerel) and is present on every table and in every order. There is no vegan dashi option and no way to avoid fish contact.

No allergen menu, staff allergy protocol, or allergy inquiry option has been noted in any review or official source. The counter operates a high-volume self-service ticket machine format with limited staff interaction.
Extremely straightforward menu — only a handful of items — so what you see is what you get; no hidden complex sauces beyond the house dashi and Worcestershire-style sauce.
Wheat noodles are boiled in shared water for every bowl; karaage (fried chicken) and gyoza are also on the menu, adding further wheat exposure throughout the kitchen.
The signature table-side condiment is a house-made ginger soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No tamari or wheat-free soy sauce alternative has been mentioned in any source.
Broth is chicken-and-pork chintan; animal stock is present in every soup bowl. There is no plant-based broth option on the menu.
天ぷら・油物メニューあり（「塩のみで」との記述はあるが専用フライヤーの使用有無は未確認）。小麦を含む揚げ物と同一厨房・フライヤーを共有している可能性がある。
懐石料理の標準的な調理で醤油（小麦含有）が煮物・タレ・だし等に使用されると推定される。グルテンフリー醤油（タマリ等）使用の明示なし。
刺身・牛肉・焼き魚・海老天ぷらなど動物性食材を同一厨房で扱うため、植物性料理との接触リスクがある。ビーガン専用調理設備の記述なし。
「ヘルシーメニューご相談」との表記あり（ぐるなびページ）。完全予約制のため、予約時に食物アレルギー・食事制限を事前相談できる環境にある。ただしアレルギー対応の専門的な体制や認証の記載はなし。
完全予約制で少人数制のため、事前に食の制限を伝える余地がある。オーナーが素材を個別に選んでいる小規模独立店であり、融通が利きやすい可能性がある。
No dedicated fryer confirmed. Tempura (seaweed tempura documented) and other fried items appear to share cooking oil. Cross-contamination from wheat flour is a realistic risk.
Standard soy sauce (wheat-containing) used as a glaze on sashimi and likely throughout the menu. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative has been noted in any source.
Fish-based dashi is standard in Japanese izakaya cooking and is presumed present in broths, fried tofu dishes, and sauces. Shared prep surfaces in a one-person kitchen increase cross-contact risk.
No allergen menu, allergy card acceptance, or allergy-handling protocol has been documented in any review or listing. Restaurant contact: 079-263-7973.

Owner-operator cooks everything from scratch to order, meaning ingredients are freshly combined rather than prepackaged — in principle this allows ingredient-level questions to be answered by the person who actually cooks the dish.
